inputs.label: Report recipient email
inputs.description: Where daily reports and alerts are emailed (defaults to the owner)

inputs.label: Low-stock threshold (days)
inputs.description: Flag a SKU when projected days of stock left falls below this

inputs.label: Reorder lead time (days)
inputs.description: How long a restock takes — used to project stockouts

inputs.label: Stuck-order window (hours)
inputs.description: Flag orders still in processing/pending past this many hours

inputs.label: Include analytics context
inputs.description: Pull sessions and conversion rate to explain sales changes

inputs.label: Product review window (days)
inputs.description: Lookback window for the product performance review

activities.intent: Pull yesterday's sales totals and comparison periods from the store platform
steps: Read the store connection; it resolves whichever platform the company runs
Pull the reporting day's orders with totals, refunds, and discounts from the store
Mark any figure the store cannot return as not available rather than estimating it
Compute yesterday's revenue, order count, and average order value
Pull the same metrics for the prior day, the prior same weekday, and the trailing 30-day daily average
Subtract refunds and total discounts to compute net revenue and discount load percent
Return a structured sales block with every figure paired to its comparison basis

activities.intent: Add traffic and conversion context to explain the day's sales movement
steps: If use_analytics is no, or no analytics connection is bound, skip this activity and continue
Resolve the store's analytics property through the analytics connection
Pull sessions, users, and ecommerce conversion rate for the reporting day and comparison periods
Compare conversion and session trends against the sales block from pull-sales
Diagnose any revenue change as fewer visitors versus a lower conversion rate and state which
Return a short context block; if analytics is unavailable, mark it skipped rather than blocking the report

activities.intent: Compile and deliver the daily sales report with movers and a watch list
steps: Build the headline line: revenue, orders, and AOV each with delta and comparison basis
Rank top movers up and down by revenue impact using the sales block
Fold in the traffic-context block to explain the day's direction in one read
Assemble a watch list of stuck orders, failed payments, and low-stock SKUs if any were surfaced by other workflows
Write the single most important action for the day as a one-line read
If the day is clean and within normal range, produce a one-line all-clear instead of padded sections
Send the report to report_recipient by email, defaulting to the owner
Emit report.ready with the headline metrics, mover lists, and watch list

activities.intent: Scan the order pipeline for stuck, failed, and unfulfilled paid orders
steps: Read the store connection; it resolves whichever platform the company runs
Pull the order pipeline: processing, pending, on-hold, failed, and paid-but-unfulfilled
Confirm fulfillment and tracking on paid orders
Flag any order state the store cannot return rather than inferring it
Flag orders stuck past stuck_processing_hours and on-hold orders past 72 hours
Flag paid orders with no fulfillment or tracking past the threshold and any failed or pending-capture payments
Detect recent refunds, chargebacks, and repeated failed attempts from one customer
Apply the alert cooldown so an already-reported issue is not re-flagged unless it crossed a worse threshold
Return a structured issue list with order ID, state, age, customer, and amount

activities.intent: Notify the owner of new order issues with full context
steps: If the issue list is empty, do nothing and end the run silently
Sort issues by impact: oldest stuck orders and highest-value failed payments first
Summarize each issue with order ID, state, age, customer, amount, and the likely cause
Group issues by type so stuck orders, failed payments, and unfulfilled paid orders are clearly separated
Email the alert to report_recipient by email, defaulting to the owner
Emit order.issue with the full issue list so a support or fulfillment agent can intervene

activities.intent: Project days of stock left per SKU from current inventory and sell-through
steps: Read the store connection; it resolves whichever platform the company runs
Pull current stock per SKU and variant from the store
Compute a trailing daily sell-through rate per SKU from recent order volume and divide current stock by it for days of stock left
Flag any SKU projected to hit zero before reorder_lead_time_days elapses or below low_stock_days
Rank flagged SKUs by velocity-weighted urgency so fast movers outrank slow movers
Apply the alert cooldown so an unchanged low-stock SKU is not re-alerted within the window
Return the ranked low-stock list with SKU, current stock, days left, and velocity

activities.intent: Notify the owner of SKUs approaching stockout
steps: If no SKU crossed the threshold, do nothing and end the run silently
Format the low-stock list sorted by soonest-to-zero with days left and reorder urgency
Call out any SKU projected to stock out before lead time as a hard reorder-now flag
Include each SKU's current stock and trailing velocity so the reorder quantity is obvious
Email the alert to report_recipient by email, defaulting to the owner
Emit inventory.low with SKU, current stock, days of stock left, and velocity for an ordering agent

activities.intent: Rank products by revenue, units, and trend over the review window
steps: Read the review_window_days input
Pull per-product sales, catalog, and any cost data from the store for the window
Mark any per-product figure the store cannot return as not available
Compute units and revenue per product for the current window and the prior equal window
Identify top performers by revenue and units with trend, and decliners that sold last period and dropped sharply this one
Identify dead stock: products with inventory and zero sales over the window
Where cost data exists, rank by contribution margin so low-margin high-volume items are not mistaken for winners
Return ranked performer, decliner, and dead-stock lists with numbers

activities.intent: Add product-level traffic and conversion context where analytics is available
steps: If use_analytics is no, or no analytics connection is bound, skip this activity and continue
Resolve the store's analytics property through the analytics connection
Pull product or landing-page sessions and conversion over the review window
Flag products with high traffic but low conversion as merchandising or pricing problems
Flag declining products whose drop is explained by lost traffic versus lost conversion
Return a context block; if analytics is unavailable, mark it skipped without blocking the review

activities.intent: Compile and deliver the weekly product performance review
steps: Lead with the week's top performers by revenue and by margin with trend
Surface decliners as the priority section since they are the silent revenue leaks
List dead stock with current inventory value tied up
Fold in the traffic-context block to diagnose decliners and underperformers
Recommend concrete actions: promote, discount to clear, reorder, or retire
Send the review to report_recipient by email, defaulting to the owner
Emit report.ready with the ranked lists and recommended actions

activities.intent: Give an on-demand snapshot of sales, open issues, and low stock right now
steps: Read the store connection; it resolves whichever platform the company runs
Pull today's running revenue, order count, and AOV with comparison to the same point on prior days
Scan the order pipeline for any currently stuck, failed, or unfulfilled paid orders
Pull current stock and compute days of stock left for the fastest-moving SKUs
Assemble a one-screen snapshot: sales headline, open issues count with worst offenders, low-stock SKUs by days left
Sort every section by impact and finish with the single most important action right now
If everything is within normal range, return a concise all-clear
